newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares surge 4.57 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares surge 4.57 pct to new record.

text.p: Turkish shares soared an average 4.57 percent on Wednesday in a continued rally further buoyed by privatisation hopes, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at this year's fifth consequtive all-time high of 1,144, up 50 points from Tuesday's previous record of 1,094. Gains totalled 17.2 percent since the market reopened on January 2 after a five-day New Year holiday.
In dollar terms, the index also hit a record of $1.04, after yesterday's $1 which equalled the previous April 8, 1996 record.
"The uptrend will remain intact with intermittent profit-taking. The index may reach 1,200 levels in coming days amid lively selective trade," sid Haldun Sertel from Can securities.
Trade volume jumped to 27.34 trillion lira from Tuesday's 20.18 trillion.
Buying accelerated in the afternoon on remarks by Turkey's privatisation chief that sell-offs would be speeded up in 1997, following a 2.38 percent rise to a midday high of 1,120 in the morning.

"Hectic activity spilled over to the whole market from largely state-owned shares and other bluechips which were initially boosted by privatisation news at the start of the second session," said Nermin Samiloglu from Tacirler securities.

Ismail Karakaya, head of the privatisation administration OIB said Turkey planned to sell an additional stake in flat steel producer Eregli in domestic and international markets after the ongoing tender for the block sale of a 30-40 percent state stake in the company.
He said Turk Telekom would be privatised in the second half of 1997 and a $500 million revenue was expected in January from the sell-off of Etibank which was split into three banks.
Karakaya also said an automatic pricing mechanism for fuel oil would take effect after the legal process has been completed to pave the way for the privatisation of state refiner Tupras.
Largely state-owned firms, namely Eregli are highly capitalised and therefore can move the index strongly.

Top actives were Eregli, up 750 lira at 14,500, utilities Cukurova Elektrik, up 7,500 lira at 145,000 and Aktas Elektrik, up 5,000 lira at 106,000, Koc Holding, up 500 lira at 22,750 and Tupras, up 3,500 lira at 30,500.
Together, they made up 24 percent of the total turnover.
Lower money and bond market rates, subdued currency trade and 1996 profit prospects of ompanies were the major factors behind the stock market's uptrend since the beginning of 1997.
T-bill and bond yields have plunged by around 20 percentage points since end-1996 to below 100 percent, excluding witholding tax, for the first time in more than a year.

Of the 233 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 166 to 39 and 28 finished steady. The IMKB Industrial gained 2.43 percent to 1,180, the IMKB Services surged 7.01 percent to 1,222, the IMKB Finacial soared six percent to 1,113.
